messages:
sam-support: FYI customer AcmeReports hitting sustained throughput drop on Dedicated pool dp-prod-7, seeing burst of 429s and long tail latencies ~2-3s per token. Reporting started ~6:20 UTC.

alex-runtime: ack. any tenant id / model / recent deploys?

sam-support: tenant acme-reports, model redwood/gpt-medium-v2 (quantized), no deploys from them. They say it started after autoscale policy tweak yesterday.

oncall-bot: ALERT: dp-prod-7 utilization spike detected 2026-03-12T06:19:42Z - queue length 320, avg batch size 2.1, drop rate 7% :rotating_light:

ravi-scheduler: copying logs could help. Also curious about max_batch_tokens + continuous_batch_window settings. small batches + high token ceiling = many microbatches.

maya-sre: noisy-tenant hypothesis: if one tenant sends lots of short requests it fragments queues and forces GPU context switches. Can we get per-tenant request-size histogram?

dave-runtime: can you paste a sample of the failing request headers + response 429 body? Also any recent scheduler commits in the last 24h?

sam-support: pasted snippet from customer: ```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer ****
Content-Length: 512
Body: {"prompt":"short user prompt","max_tokens":512,"temperature":0.0}

Response: 429 {"error":"rate_limited","retry_after_ms":125} 
```

alex-runtime: interesting - Content-Length small but max_tokens large => server preallocates max token slots, causing small prompts to be split across token buckets? needs deeper look.

ravi-scheduler: right. If continuous_batcher groups strictly by token ceiling, few short prompts with big max_tokens cause packing inefficiency. Check scheduler param `max_batch_tokens_per_gpu` and `batch_window_ms`. If window is tiny, packing is poor.

maya-sre: metrics: dp-prod-7 reports avg_batch_utilization 28% in last 3h, prefill_wait_ms spiked. Also autoscale didn't add nodes because scale_up_trigger based on average_utilization > 80% but util per-node stayed artificially low due to fragmentation.

dave-runtime: propose repro: run a load test that mixes many small requests with large max_tokens to mimic customer. Use this quick script:```python
# repro_load.py
import requests, time, random
URL='https://dp-prod-7.api.redwood/v1/generate'
HEAD={'Authorization':'Bearer XXX'}
for i in range(2000):
    payload={'prompt':'hi','max_tokens':random.choice([16,256,512])}
    r=requests.post(URL,json=payload,headers=HEAD,timeout=10)
    if r.status_code==429: print('429 at',i)
    time.sleep(0.005)
```
Run from a few clients to reproduce.

ravi-scheduler: thanks. Short-term mitigation: reduce `max_batch_tokens_per_gpu` so scheduler prefers larger batches by token rather than microbatch count, or increase `batch_window_ms` from 10->50ms for dp-prod-7 pool. Either should increase pack efficiency and push avg_utilization up.

alex-runtime: can we try a config change in canary: dp-prod-7-zone-a only? Change `batch_window_ms=50` and `prefill_timeout_ms=20` and monitor packing. If packing improves, scale signals will reflect true utilization and autoscale will add capacity if needed.

maya-sre: created canary config draft and applied to zone-a. Watching metrics. prefill_wait_ms dropped 40% after 2m, avg_batch_size rose from 2.1->3.9.

oncall-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: applied canary batch_window_ms=50 to dp-prod-7-zone-a by maya-sre at 2026-03-12T06:36:12Z

sam-support: customer reports 429s reduced to intermittent, latency improved for most requests. They still see some 429 bursts during traffic spikes.

dave-runtime: followups: 1) add per-tenant token histogram to dashboard (short term alert) 2) consider scheduler heuristic: prefer packing by token_sum instead of request_count when variance of max_tokens > threshold 3) add a tenant isolation knob for noisy tenants to cap concurrency.

ravi-scheduler: I'll open a PR for heuristic change and include unit tests + simulation harness. For immediate hotfix we can roll batch_window increase to remaining zones after 30m observation.

maya-sre: agreed. rolling to zone-b now. keep an eye on autoscale triggers.

oncall-bot: ROLL: batch_window_ms=50 rolled to dp-prod-7-zone-b by maya-sre at 2026-03-12T07:02:01Z

sam-support: customer confirmed steady state improved. logging follow-up: please capture a 10m request sample for tenant acme-reports and attach to ticket so we can root cause whether they changed client behavior.

alex-runtime: note for postmortem: add a section on "batch token fragmentation" and include recommended default batch_window_ms for Dedicated pools with heterogeneous max_tokens workloads.

dave-runtime: leaving next steps in ticket: PR link + canary metrics + customer sample. thanks all :thumbsup:
